note: How densely a vocal can carry syllables. A profile supplies two things: `band`, the syllables-per-line guidance the writing brief states, and the two rate ceilings that decide whether a section can physically hold what was written. They are different numbers on purpose -- the band is where good writing usually sits, the ceiling is where the clock runs out.
derivation: The mid-tempo profile's band is the generator's own documented recommendation of 6-10 syllables per line. The ceilings are calibrated against the structure templates: at 95 BPM a one-bar line is 2.53s, so the band's upper end needs about 4.0 syllables/s if a line occupies a single bar, and about 2.0 if it occupies two. sung_mid's ceiling of 3.2 sits between those, which is the intended reading -- a template that gives two bars per line has headroom, and a writer who crams a line into one bar does not. These are estimates from arithmetic and the model's own guidance, not measurements of a singer, so every rate they produce is reported as approximate.
